clue.text: Town's serenades interrupting cook

indicators.note: the serenading breaks into the middle of the cooking word, splitting it in two

parts.note: to cook is to bake
someone who serenades sings to their beloved

explanation.surface: Musicians break into song while someone is busy in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay. 'Serenades' must be read as a two-word verb phrase, which 'interrupting' places inside the kitchen word.
explanation.definitionFit: Basingstoke is a large town in Hampshire, southern England.

clue.text: See me repeatedly boo a Britney pop song that she sings

indicators.note: pop here means burst apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt
the word me is said more than once, giving it twice over

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a crowd jeer at a pop star's performance of her hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like part of 'pop song' but is the anagram signal for MEME BOO A BRITNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Britney Spears's 1998 debut single was titled with these words, so it is a song she sings.

clue.text: Bristly bits must be regularly extracted from sweet face

indicators.note: every other letter is drawn out of the two words, at a regular interval

explanation.surface: A grooming tip: stray bristles must be plucked from a pretty face now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Setae are the stiff bristles or hairs found on worms, insects and some plants.

clue.text: Hurried up with the cross somewhere in church?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: hurried means ran
taken as written
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Someone rushed up the aisle carrying the cross to a spot in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A narthex is the entrance hall or porch at the west end of a church, so it is one place inside one.

clue.text: In love and almost ecstatic holding hand

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps round the other, keeping it inside
almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: sent is old slang for ecstatic or carried away
a mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Lovers so happy they can't stop holding hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final letter of the slang word for ecstatic, and 'holding' wraps what is left round the hand word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be smitten is to be struck with love or infatuation.

clue.text: Cell consisting of three round objects

parts.note: an O is round, as is a sphere
a second O, a second round shape
a sphere is a round object, the third of the three

explanation.surface: A cell described as made up of three balls.
explanation.walkthrough: The three round objects are O, O and SPHERE side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An oosphere is the unfertilised female reproductive cell of some algae and fungi.

clue.text: Baronet, hairy man, frightful beast on Greek mountain

indicators.note: frightful suggests something awfully disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of monsters: a nobleman, a hairy fellow and a terrible creature from a Greek peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' seems to describe the beast but rearranges BARONET HAIRY MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Erymanthian boar lived on Mount Erymanthos; Heracles captured it as his fourth labour.

clue.text: One's ending with muck around one — as a result of this?

definitions.text: One's ending with muck around one — as a result of this?

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is the one taken
the dirt word goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: muck means mess
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone ends up covered in filth, and the clue asks what caused it.
explanation.walkthrough: E (the last letter of 'One') plus MESS round I. The whole clue also describes being sick and finishing up in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Emesis is the medical term for vomiting, which can leave someone covered in muck.

clue.text: Support brilliant objective

parts.note: def is slang for excellent or brilliant
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: Backing a fine goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend something is to back it up or uphold it.

clue.text: Original film with old boy knocking out a US criminal

indicators.note: one piece knocks out the letter a and takes its place

parts.note: a master is the original copy of a film from which others are made
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A classic movie in which a retired gent knocks out an American villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is the letter knocked out of MASTER, so OB replaces it: M + OB + STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobster is a gangster, a member of an organised criminal gang in America.

clue.text: Trendy person of faith has rejected cathedral impressively

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy person

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, crosswords' usual cathedral

explanation.surface: A fashionable believer has turned against a cathedral in some grand way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trendy' looks like the definition but gives IN; the definition is at the other end. ELY backwards is YLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something in style is to do it with flair, impressively.

clue.text: Bird that's cold entering a hot nest after flying

indicators.note: the cold letter goes inside the rearranged letters
flying suggests things sent scattering, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A bird that has caught a chill finds a warm nest after its flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after flying' scrambles the three words that follow 'entering', and the cold letter slips into the middle of that rearrangement. The surface's warm nest is pure decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small European bird of the thrush family, named for its call like stones knocking.

clue.text: Big effort brings supreme happiness, all but

indicators.note: all but means everything except the last letter

parts.note: heaven is a state of supreme bliss

explanation.surface: Trying hard produces near-perfect joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A heave is a strong pull or push, a great physical exertion.

clue.text: Little girl facing the unknown in a place of great crisis

parts.note: Sue is a short form of the girl's name Susan
Z is used in algebra for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A small child confronting an uncertain future in a disaster zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the Suez Crisis of 1956, when Britain and France invaded Egypt over the canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suez Canal zone was the scene of a major international crisis in 1956.

clue.text: No longer individual gets slated, being pronounced innocent

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
one means a single individual
rated means told off or scolded, as slated does

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost their identity is criticised before being cleared in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slated' and RATED both mean scolded harshly, though RATED here is an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exonerated is to be officially cleared of blame or declared not guilty.

clue.text: Spooner's ungainly person to fix down in part of ship

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: a hulk is a big clumsy person
to bed something is to fix it firmly in place

explanation.surface: A clumsy fellow trying to secure something below decks.
explanation.walkthrough: HULK BED becomes BULK HED, whose second half sounds like HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulkhead is a dividing wall between compartments in a ship's hull.

clue.text: Spread to excite gourmet and pal

indicators.note: excite means stir up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rumour put about to get a foodie and his friend worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like food for a gourmet but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To promulgate is to make widely known or proclaim, to spread an idea.

clue.text: Mathematician from China embracing a leading pair of scientists

indicators.note: the friend word hugs the other letters inside it

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), hence pal

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A mathematician from China takes in two leading scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like a country but is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate. 'leading pair of' takes two letters, and 'embracing' wraps the mate word round them with A.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise Pascal was a 17th-century French mathematician and philosopher.

clue.text: One may produce smile, not half, going about stage being funny

definitions.text: One may produce smile, not half, going about stage being funny

indicators.note: the shortened smile word goes round the other letters
not half means only half the word is kept

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile

indicators.note: being funny means acting oddly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comic on stage who raises a half-smile by fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' halves the smile word, 'being funny' scrambles STAGE, and 'going about' puts the half round the scramble. Read whole, the clue describes a stage joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is a comedian who tells jokes, someone who gets laughs.

clue.text: Emotional rugby group left after meal

indicators.note: the rugby and left letters come after the meal word

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in parts of Britain
RFU is the Rugby Football Union, which runs English rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby team gets weepy after their dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tearful is crying or close to tears, showing strong feeling.

clue.text: Pasquale's an artist, first to last!

indicators.note: the opening letter is shifted to the end

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being an artist, putting himself first and last.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter Pasquale refers to himself, so his possession is 'mine'. EMIN with E moved gives MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken by the setter, Pasquale's belongings are what he would call his own.

clue.text: Car with Spanish identification, say

parts.note: E is the international vehicle registration code for Spain
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A vehicle with a Spanish number plate, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like an 'for example' marker but gives STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a British car with a long body and rear door, called a station wagon in the US.

clue.text: Glossy boats from stern to bow

indicators.note: reading from the back of a vessel to the front means taking the word backwards

parts.note: keels are boats, in a poetic or old sense

explanation.surface: Shiny vessels described from end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek means smooth and shiny, glossy in appearance.

clue.text: Oppose profits pocketed by stupid person?

indicators.note: the profits go inside the other word, as into a pocket

parts.note: a goat is a foolish person
gains are profits

explanation.surface: Objecting to a fool lining his pockets with profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketed by' puts the profits inside the fool word, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To go against something is to resist or act contrary to it.

clue.text: A set of directions hardly used

parts.note: S, N, E and W are the compass points south, north, east and west

explanation.surface: A set of instructions that has barely been touched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' looks like instructions but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as new is in nearly perfect condition, almost unused.

clue.text: Nourishment from fruit worker's consumed

indicators.note: the worker has swallowed the fruit, so it goes inside

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect; the 's is 'has'
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Food from a fruit that a labourer has eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or nourishment.

clue.text: Learn to have admirable scepticism when listening

indicators.note: listening means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: admirable means fine, and scepticism means doubt

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a healthy suspicion when hearing things.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out is to discover or come to know a fact.

clue.text: Andy rather than Grant providing ingredient for home-made wine?

definitions.text: Andy rather than Grant providing ingredient for home-made wine?

parts.words: Andy rather than Grant providing ingredient for home-made wine
parts.note: Andy and Grant Flower were brothers who played cricket for Zimbabwe, and Andy was born first; that older brother's surname plus his seniority names a blossom used in wine-making

explanation.walkthrough: Andy Flower and his younger brother Grant were Zimbabwe Test cricketers, so Andy is the older of the Flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossoms of the elder tree are used to make cordial and country wines at home.
